answer: In an attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so influence from any identity is limited by the probability that those walks reach it. A sybil cluster may look internally dense, like a canyon sheltering a sparrow, yet its sparse external cut gives it low conductance: few edges carry trust across the boundary. With normalized transition weights and bounded walk length, this bottleneck constrains the cluster’s aggregate voting weight; an honest beacon cannot be replaced merely by multiplying identities.
